summary: Azul is a light, tactile tile-drafting game where you snake-draft colored tiles into staging rows and then transfer them onto a wall to score points, with the tension coming from denying opponents useful colors and managing overflow penalties. It plays fast, looks gorgeous on the table, and rewards short-term tactical planning more than deep strategy.
praised: Beautiful, tactile components (the tiles feel great to handle)
Easy to teach and quick to play
Satisfying push-your-luck tension between grabbing tiles you need and dumping unwanted colors on opponents
Scales well and works as a gateway/family game
criticised: Can feel too abstract or 'mathy' for players wanting theme
Runaway leader potential is low but a single bad round can be very punishing
Limited long-term strategic depth once the pattern is learned
Some find it a bit solitaire-ish at 2 players compared to 3-4

interaction.kind: blocking and area denial via tile drafting

win_criteria: Most points, one or two sources

scoring.why: Wall-tile placement adjacency bonuses plus end-game row/column/color completion bonuses decide the winner, while floor-line penalties for overflow tiles punish poor drafting.
